name: Col of the Wild
text: [overview] brief cruxes of ice or mixed rock appear now and then, with much simulclimbing on steep snow.
[overview] Near the top a large cornice may need tunneling.
[detailed_rack] Standard alpine rack: some small and medium cams, a nut selection, knifeblades, angles, screws for ice, specters and a few pickets.
earlierWhy: Long snow route; text silent on glacier travel.

name: Kissing up the choss pile
text: [approach] From the Reed Lakes lot, walk to the former building site, short of Nugget Boulder and the Snowbird slab.
[approach] Then take the path bearing left up the drainage, past the Snowbird mine on your right, and keep going up the bowls to the pass.
[approach] The Snowbird Glacier lies below the pass, and the Nunatak is the small formation beside it.
earlierWhy: Beside a small Alaska glacier below a pass; crevassing unknown.

name: The Friends Along the Way
text: [overview] A couloir with over 2500 feet of gain, with snow close to vertical and traverses over chossy rock sections.
[overview] The first fork: steep snow if you go right, then 50 feet of steep choss;
[overview] going left means far steeper snow and some snow bridges.
[detailed_rack] A rope and a skeleton rack are worth carrying if snow anchors for descending are within your skills.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — required
earlierWhy: Steep couloir with snow bridges; glacier not stated.

name: Smoke em' if you got em'
text: [overview] Pitches 1-3 are the couloir (simul-climbing is possible depending on snow quality);
[detailed_rack] 3-6 snow pickets, cams from .5 to #2, and a full set of nuts.
earlierWhy: Snow couloir start; glacier not stated.

name: Splitter Choss
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — optional for the approach
earlierWhy: Snow gear optional on approach; glacier not stated.

name: North Gully
text: [overview] Turning right gives the main gully, snow with WI2 steps to the top;
[overview] Descent options: by way of Thunder-East Glacier, steep creek, or downclimbing or rappelling the gully.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws, and perhaps a picket or two.
earlierWhy: Descent may use a glacier; the ascent line is snow gully.

name: West Ridge
text: [descent_text] From the summit, put on crampons and descend west on snow or ice until the scree slopes leading toward Twincicle Pass appear.
[descent_text] Go down through Twincicle Pass and the Twincicle Valley, which is a tangle of alders, and cross the short but very steep Twincicle Glacier.
earlierWhy: Descent crosses a short steep glacier.

name: West Twincil
text: [overview] alternatively stop above and climb a near-vertical snow step 10-20 ft tall to a ledge, from which a wider couloir continues to the basin below.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow and complex avalanche terrain;
[detailed_rack] consult snow and avalanche forecasts beforehand.
[approach] The line is steep, narrow and avalanche-prone, so it is best entered in very stable conditions after studying the map and the snow.
earlierWhy: Steep avalanche couloir; glacier not stated.

name: Gog East Face
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.
earlierWhy: It crosses a snowfield and a moat below the face; searches did not say whether the Echo Glacier side is crevassed.

name: Magog
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Hike across the snowfield to the east face and cross the moat to rock below the notch between the two summits.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk back down the snowfield toward the hut.
earlierWhy: It crosses a snowfield and a moat to the east face; searches did not settle crevasse hazard.

name: Mount Quadrant West Face to North Summit (Stem-winder)
text: [overview] Snow may cover the approach and return.

[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the Friendship Col trail until it turns up the snow slopes toward Gog and Magog, then continue straight over the ridge, drop down and around the left side of the lake, and climb back up to the base of Quadrant's north face.
[approach] There is some snow on the approach.
earlierWhy: The text only mentions some snow on the approach, and searches gave no detail on its season or any glacier.

name: Another Fine Day in The Bugaboos
text: [overview] After a short moat pitch, pitches 1 to 3 (5.7) trend through cracks and corners beside a gendarme.
[approach] Cross snow and scree beneath the east buttress of Brenta Spire toward its northeast spur;
[approach] the route begins from the snow in a moat at the foot of that spur.
[descent_text] a short scramble and a final rappel lead into a moat, so an ice axe is useful.
earlierWhy: The text mentions snow, a moat and an axe being useful, which does not settle glacier travel or season.

name: Kiss of Death (Sinnes Couloir)
text: [detailed_rack] Conditions are steep snow or neve, with no ice.
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.
earlierWhy: It is a steep snow or neve couloir, and the text does not say whether a glacier is on the line.

name: Stanford Route
text: [approach] Climbers start from a high camp at the saddle northeast of the peak, from which a snow ridge rises to a subsummit.
earlierWhy: The route climbs a snow ridge from a high camp in a glaciated range, and the search found no glacier detail.

name: East Ridge
text: [hazards] Snow or glacier cover early in the season
[gear] Ice axe and crampons if snow or ice remains
earlierWhy: The text mentions snow or glacier cover only for early season.

name: Arete Du Phalanx (Phalanx South Arete)
text: [overview] The initial half is mostly 3rd/4th class, snow or rock, ending at a prominent spire: sling it, then either rappel or downclimb, and cross steep snow rightward.
[overview] Beyond, the narrow aesthetic arete (low 5th) can be bypassed by an easier traverse, up and to the right across steep snow.
[overview] The final ridge brings further steep snow plus easy mixed ground.
earlierWhy: The route crosses steep snow in places, and glacier was not checked.

name: Northeast Buttress (Up In Smoke)
text: [overview] The lower buttress takes roughly 16 to 18 pitches of rock at mid-5th standard (up to 5.7) on the crest's left side, ending at the mid-height snowpatch.
[overview] Three pitches climb the lowest ice arete, which is low-angle and likely just snow early in the season;
earlierWhy: The buttress is on a peak beside the Monarch Icefield and ends at a mid-height snowpatch, but I found no description of the approach.

name: Austrian Arete
text: [overview] One to two pitches short of the summit area the arete flattens (4th class and some snow).
[detailed_rack] carry an axe and crampons for the descent.
earlierWhy: Axe and crampons are carried for the descent and snow is on the arete; the glacier question is not settled.
